observation.visible_scene: A wide, low-angle view of a flat grassland plain under a massive, dark storm cloud (cumulonimbus) that fills most of the frame. A small mesa sits on the left horizon and a warm, golden band of light glows along the right horizon, indicating low sun. A vertical rain/virga curtain hangs from the cloud base on the right side, with a brighter, light-catching patch of precipitation near the center of the horizon. The ground and horizon line remain in fixed positions throughout.
visible_changes: The dark cloud mass slowly reorganizes and deforms rather than translating as a rigid block; its internal lobes and shading shift gradually from frame 1 to frame 41.

Streaky, radiating cloud bands (roll/mammatus-like striations) become progressively more defined on the left portion of the cloud, especially from the middle frames onward, where they fan diagonally toward the center.

The rain curtain on the right changes appearance: it is a darker, more uniform sheet early on and becomes broader, lighter, and more diffuse toward the end, while the bright light-lit rain patch near the center horizon shifts slightly and softens.
The overall cloud outline on the right recedes somewhat as the precipitation area spreads, altering the silhouette against the bright horizon.

The foreground grassland, the left mesa, and the horizon line stay at the same image positions, consistent with a static (non-panning) camera; the observed motion is cloud/rain evolution, not camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the storm is approaching, passing, or receding relative to the camera, and the full lifecycle of the cloud.
Whether the visible precipitation actually reaches the ground or is virga.
The wind field driving the cloud deformation and the conditions before t=0 or after t=2.67 s.
Any lightning or gust-front activity outside this segment.
uncertain_details: Exact net direction and speed of the cloud's drift are hard to pin down because most change is internal deformation rather than clear translation.
Minor camera vibration or reframing cannot be fully ruled out, though the fixed horizon suggests it is essentially static.
The distinction between the bright central rain patch and the right-side rain curtain as separate features versus one continuous shaft is partly ambiguous.

the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
